title: Volume and surface area of composite solids
summary: Combine component measures and remove overlaps, holes or hidden faces.
objectives: Add or subtract component volumes without double-counting.
Remove two copies of each hidden contact face from surface area.
Solve multi-step capacity and material problems involving composite solids.

blocks.text: Combine component measures and remove overlaps, holes or hidden faces. Keep every measurement in compatible units before substituting.

For a composite solid, volume is additive for joined non-overlapping pieces and subtractive for holes. Surface area requires a face audit: count exposed faces only. When two solids are joined, the contact region disappears from the outside surface on both pieces.

Sketch an exploded view or table of components. Calculate each component volume using consistent units. For surface area, start with the separate totals and subtract twice the contact area. For a drilled hole, subtract its volume and add any newly exposed inner curved surface if surface area is required.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Two cuboids of volumes 180 cm³ and 75 cm³ are joined without overlap. Find the total volume.

sections.verification_note: The result uses compatible units and agrees with the dimensions and component structure.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Two cuboids are joined across a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangular face. Their separate surface areas are 94 cm² and 112 cm². Find the exposed surface area of the composite solid.

content.text: That face was counted once on each separate cuboid, so subtract 2×12.

sections.verification_note: The joined solid has less surface area than the sum 206 cm² of the separate solids.

blocks.text: Do not subtract a contact face only once. Do not subtract contact volume when pieces merely touch. Distinguish a cavity, which creates internal exposed surfaces, from a removed block whose opening and faces must be considered explicitly.

prompt.text: A 6 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm cuboid has a 2 cm cube removed. Find the remaining volume in cm³.
